text: package follows standard Rcpp pattern: - R wrapper functions R/*.R handle input validation, formula parsing, result formatting - C++ core functions src/*.cpp perform heavy computation - Exports auto-generated src/RcppExports.cpp R/RcppExports.R via Rcpp::compileAttributes() - Internal C++ functions prefixed . title: CLAUDE.md
text: 1. Fisher-Scoring Iteration: Fay-Herriot estimation uses Fisher-scoring algorithm implemented C++ speed. algorithm iterates estimate random effect variance (sigma²), computes EBLUPs. 2. Spatial Weight Matrix: Spatial models require row-standardized proximity matrix W. spatial models, matrix must cover domains (including unsampled), just sampled ones—code handles unsampled areas borrowing strength spatial neighbors. 3. Bootstrap Parallelization: Parametric non-parametric bootstrap MSE use OpenMP via RcppParallel. n_threads parameter controls parallelism; n_threads = 0 uses available cores. 4. Unsampled Domain Handling: - Fay-Herriot (eblup_fh): Uses synthetic estimators areas NA response - Spatial FH (eblup_sfh): Uses spatial kriging (full-spatial synthetic) unsampled areas - Spatio-Temporal FH (eblup_stfh): support unsampled domains (complete panel required) 5. Output Structure: fitting functions return list class fastsae containing: - df_eblup: Data frame estimates (eblup, mse, rse) - estcoef: Regression coefficients SE, z-value, p-value - random_effect_var: Estimated variance random effects - goodness: Log-likelihood, AIC, BIC - n_iter, convergence: Convergence information

what: Architectural Insights: Why is fastsae so Fast?
title: Performance & Scalability Benchmarks
text: Compiled C++ Linear Solvers: Instead interpreting nested loops R, fastsae implements Fisher-scoring parameter search Woodbury identity matrix inversions Armadillo C++, directly leveraging optimized BLAS/LAPACK routines. Zero-Copy Matrix Operations: Memory allocations large intermediate structures (VV, V−1V^{-1}, PP) avoided reused across Fisher iterations rather reallocated heap. OpenMP Multi-Threaded Bootstrap: Bootstrap resampling runs natively parallel across CPU cores using #pragma omp parallel , avoiding serialization overhead R worker processes (parallel::makeCluster / foreach). Woodbury Identity Panel Data: eblup_stfh, inversion block (DT×DT)(DT \times DT) covariance matrix VV reduced operations individual D×DD \times D T×TT \times T blocks via Kronecker Woodbury decomposition, transforming O((DT)3)O((DT)^3) bottleneck scalable O(D3+T3)O(D^3 + T^3) steps.

text: Spatial Fay-Herriot model (Pratesi & Salvati, 2008) models area random effects using Simultaneous Autoregressive (SAR(1)) process: y=Xβ+u+ey = X\beta + u + e u=ρ1Wu+ϵ1⟹u=(−ρ1W)−1ϵ1u = \rho_1 W u + \epsilon_1 \implies u = (- \rho_1 W)^{-1} \epsilon_1 : - WW known row-standardized spatial proximity matrix (D×DD \times D). - ρ1∈(−1,1)\rho_1 \(-1, 1) spatial autoregressive parameter. - ϵ1∼N(0,σu12ID)\epsilon_1 \sim N(0, \sigma_{u1}^2 I_D) independent innovation noise. - e∼N(0,Ve)e \sim N(0, V_e) sampling error diagonal matrix Ve=diag(D1,…,DD)V_e = \text{diag}(D_1, \dots, D_D).

title: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Models
text: Spatio-Temporal model (Marhuenda, Molina, & Morales, 2013) combines spatial correlation temporal autoregression across balanced panel DD areas observed TT time periods: ydt=xdt⊤β+u1d+u2dt+edty_{dt} = x_{dt}^\top \beta + u_{1d} + u_{2dt} + e_{dt} : - u1=(u11,…,u1D)⊤u_1 = (u_{11}, \dots, u_{1D})^\top captures static spatial effects: u1=ρ1Wu1+ϵ1u_1 = \rho_1 W u_1 + \epsilon_1. - u2d=(u2d1,…,u2dT)⊤u_{2d} = (u_{2d1}, \dots, u_{2dT})^\top captures dynamic temporal effects area dd: u2dt=ρ2u2d,t−1+ϵ2dtu_{2dt} = \rho_2 u_{2d,t-1} + \epsilon_{2dt}. - edt∼ind. N(0,Ddt)e_{dt} \sim \text{ind. } N(0, D_{dt}) sampling errors.

title: Unit-Level Estimation with Battese-Harter-Fuller
text: Unlike area-level models aggregate data prior modeling, unit-level models operate directly individual survey unit records (e.g., households, farms, persons) linking population auxiliary aggregates (e.g., census means satellite imagery). fastsae package implements nested error regression model Battese, Harter, Fuller (1988) via eblup_bhf(), providing fast estimation parallel parametric bootstrap MSE.

title: Unit-Level Estimation with Battese-Harter-Fuller
text: individual unit jj (j=1,…,ndj = 1, \dots, n_d) small area dd (d=1,…,Dd = 1, \dots, D): ydj=xdj⊤β+ud+edjy_{dj} = x_{dj}^\top \beta + u_d + e_{dj} : - ud∼..d. N(0,σu2)u_d \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_u^2) area-specific random effect. - edj∼..d. N(0,σe2)e_{dj} \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_e^2) unit-level error variance. - udu_d edje_{dj} mutually independent. small area population mean Y‾d\bar{Y}_d estimated : Y‾̂dEBLUP=X‾d⊤β̂+γd(y‾d−x‾d⊤β̂)\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{EBLUP}} = \bar{X}_d^\top \hat{\beta} + \gamma_d (\bar{y}_d - \bar{x}_d^\top \hat{\beta}) : - X‾d\bar{X}_d known population mean vector auxiliary variables domain dd. - y‾d\bar{y}_d x‾d\bar{x}_d sample means domain dd. - γd=σu2σu2+σe2/nd\gamma_d = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2 / n_d} shrinkage ratio.
